**Analysis summary:**
- Test image: Lodged corn plant with **purple/reddish-dark stalk discoloration**, dried tan leaves
- Anthracnose stalk rot: causes dark, purplish-black discoloration of the stalk rind — characteristic signature of *Colletotrichum graminicola* on the stalk exterior
- Charcoal stalk rot: internal fibrous dry rot, gray/beige — no purple coloring
- Diplodia stalk rot: tan/brown stalks, no purple coloring
- Bacterial stalk rot: water-soaked slimy lesions

The prominent purple/reddish-purple coloration of the stalk with plant lodging is the hallmark of Anthracnose stalk rot.
